key_insight: HSE’s screened hybrid design made exact exchange practical for solids and unexpectedly delivered much better band gaps than semilocal functionals, while preserving strong performance across chemistry and materials benchmarks.
engineering_relevance: For materials discovery and device modeling, HSE and its descendants provide a reliable middle ground between accuracy and cost for predicting band gaps, defects, and related properties in semiconductors and oxides.
method: Keep exact exchange at short range and screen it at long range to make hybrid DFT feasible for extended systems.
Use the fixed 25% exact-exchange fraction inherited from PBE0 rather than fitting directly to solids.
Compare HSE03/HSE06 and newer semilocal or hybrid variants against solid-state benchmark sets for gaps, structures, energetics, and cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HSE band gaps for ordinary semiconductors and selected oxides came out substantially closer to experiment than semilocal approximations, and that recent meta-GGAs can match HSE06 on selected semiconductors.
watch_item: Fixed screening and a fixed exchange fraction can limit transferability, so dielectric-dependent or tuned hybrids may be needed when the electronic environment varies strongly.
paper_title: Perspective: The HSE Screened Hybrid and the Band Gap Problem: Origins, Impact, and the Contenders
